notes: Summary: Orbitron builds low-latency personalization and bidding components for large ad exchanges. Primary goal is replace brittle in-house inference with a single predictable runtime that reduces cost and tightens P95 latency to sub-120ms for 512-token chat flows.

Recent discovery highlighted three optimization priorities: dynamic batching tuned to request size distribution, aggressive KV/prefix caching for repeated user context, and quantization profiles (4-bit/8-bit) that maintain quality while reducing token cost.
Quote from CTO (R. Vega): 'We need consistent tail latency — spikes kill auctions. If you can't prove sub-120ms tail at 400 qps, it's a non-starter.'

They already run a small internal benchmarking harness (Go + gRPC) and provided sample traces; results show mean latencies acceptable but 99th spikes ~350ms under synthetic load due to cold KV cache and bursty traffic patterns.
Cost sensitivity: current spend ~ $65k/mo on GPU inference. Target is 30–50% unit cost reduction via batching + quantization + strategic routing to cheaper model variants during off-peak.
Model preferences: open-model first policy — prefer quantized Llama2-13B or Mistral-7B family; want automated fallbacks to smaller quantized models for non-critical reranking paths.
Routing needs: regional routing (NA + EU), fallback to lower-cost model pool when Dedicated pool saturated, sticky KV cache per user session, per-customer isolation for B2B partners.
Compliance: EU data residency required for several publisher partners, SOC2 compliance mandated, customer wants KMS integration and retention controls for request logs.

POC ask: 2-week dedicated POC with 4x A100-equivalent reserved capacity, run Redwood perf benchmark tool across real traces, measure P50/P95/P99 and per-token cost for: vanilla float32, int8 quantized, and Q4_0 profiles. Provide tuning recipes for batching and cache TTLs.

Sales/technical notes: SE demo on 2026-01-28 (Fireflies link) — walked through batching controls and Optimize suggestions. AE proposed a scoped Optimize engagement to automate tuning for their traffic mix.
Decision timeline: CTO committed to vendor decision by 2026-04 if POC proves tail latency and cost targets. Procurement requires pricing for reserved commit (6–12 months) and SOC2 evidence.

Internal: follow-up items - provide detailed perf run plan, share recommended quantization tradeoffs (quality vs latency), offer deterministic benchmark script that replays live traces, add EU region availability confirmation.
Stated constraints: cannot accept any service that requires moving PII outside EU for publisher partners. On-prem not required today but VPC/private Dedicated is desired for isolation.
Emails: thread contains sample trace tar (attached) and internal cost model spreadsheet. AE note: 'need Redwood to reproduce our bursty 800rps 30s spike and show degradation characteristics.'

technical_requirements_summary: Workload: mixed — production chat (avg 120 tokens), reranking (short inputs), and personalization lookups (small KV reads).
Latency SLOs: P95 <= 120ms for chat 120-token flows under 400 sustained qps; P99 <= 250ms desirable.
Throughput: baseline 400 qps, peak bursts to 800 qps for 20–60s windows (auction bursts).
Cost target: 30–50% reduction vs current GPU spend through batching, quantization, and cache hit improvements.
Model strategy: primary quantized Llama2-13B / Mistral-7B; fallback to 7B-class quantized models for non-critical paths. Policy-based routing to cheaper pools at >90% capacity.

Optimization asks: recommended batch sizing policy per route, adaptive batching for burst smoothing, KV/prefix cache TTL tuning, quantization profiles (Q4_0 vs INT8) with quality loss estimates, perf test harness for repeatable runs.
Observability: token-level cost breakdown, latency histograms per route, trace-based waterfalls for P99 investigations, rollback & canary controls for model changes.
Security: SSO (SAML) + SCIM, KMS integration for key management, audit logs retention controls (90 days default, negotiable), EU data residency guardrails.
poc_scope_and_success_metrics: Duration: 2-week Dedicated POC (customer-supplied load replayer + Redwood perf tool).
Targets: P95 <= 120ms on production trace replay at 400 qps sustained; 30%+ unit cost reduction measured vs baseline run.
Runs: three benchmark runs — float baseline, int8, q4 profile; each run includes cold-start + warm-cache phases to capture prefix caching effects.
Deliverables: benchmark report (latency percentiles + per-token cost), recommended batching/cache config, quantization tradeoff matrix, short runbook for production rollout.
observation_and_risks: Risk: quality regression after aggressive quantization — will require eval set and A/B checks in Redwood Optimize.
Risk: cache warming pattern — auctions create cold-cache windows; need TTL and prefetch strategies.
Risk: procurement timeline — legal needs SOC2 evidence before commit; may delay closed-won until 2026-05 if not resolved.
